title: LORETA Neurofeedback
subtitle: Source-estimated training from scalp measurements
altText: Chalkboard-style clinical diagram illustrating loreta neurofeedback within a neurofeedback closed loop.
learningObjectives: Explain loreta neurofeedback without diagnostic overreach.
Distinguish measurement, mechanism and clinical outcome in loreta neurofeedback.
Identify one safety or validity limitation relevant to loreta neurofeedback.

sections.explainSimply: LORETA-based systems estimate distributed brain sources from scalp EEG and feed back a selected source metric.
sections.explainLikePsychologist: Source localisation is an inverse solution constrained by model assumptions, electrode density, anatomy and noise. Spatial precision should not be overstated.
sections.advancedClinicalDetail: Training a source estimate adds modelling layers between measurement and reward. Reports should specify solver, regularisation, head model and target definition.
sections.thinkOfItLike: Choosing a camera lens: every method emphasises some information and introduces its own distortions.
sections.whyPsychologistsCare: Psychologists need to understand loreta neurofeedback to evaluate mechanism claims, informed consent, treatment fit and whether change transfers to real-world function.
sections.whenItGoesWrong: A colourful 3D source image is not direct intracranial measurement.
sections.clinicalPearl: The trained metric is an intermediate target; the clinical endpoint is meaningful function.
sections.practicalExample: A clinician using loreta neurofeedback predefines the target, checks raw signal and artifacts, monitors symptoms and function, and reviews whether change generalises beyond the feedback display.
sections.limitationsCautions: A colourful 3D source image is not direct intracranial measurement. Evidence classification: emerging; insufficient clinical evidence.
